title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 13th Congressional District
area: South-central Pennsylvania, including Altoona, Chambersburg, Gettysburg, and Ebensburg.

context.text: Incumbent Republican John Joyce and Democrat Beth Farnham both won uncontested or single-candidate primaries on May 19, 2026, and are a rematch of the 2024 general election, which Joyce won 74.1% to 25.8%.

candidates.name: John Joyce
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the May 19 Republican primary

summary.text: John Joyce is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 13th District. A physician who trained in internal medicine and dermatology and co-founded a dermatology practice in Altoona, he has served in Congress since January 2019 and chairs the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations. According to his House website, he has focused on rural health care, energy prices and rural broadband.

background.text: Born in Altoona, Pennsylvania, in 1957. His House website describes him as the second generation of the Joyce family to be born and raised in Pennsylvania.

Attended Penn State Altoona and then Pennsylvania State University (B.S., 1979), and earned his M.D. from Temple University (1983). He completed postgraduate medical training at Johns Hopkins Hospital and is board-certified in internal medicine and dermatology.
Served in the U.S. Navy during Desert Storm at Portsmouth Naval Hospital in Virginia, after six years at Johns Hopkins.
With his wife, Dr. Alice Plummer Joyce, established Altoona Dermatology Associates in 1991; the couple practiced there for more than 25 years before his election to Congress.
Won the 2018 general election for Pennsylvania's 13th District, defeating Democrat Brent Ottaway in a race with no incumbent, and took office in January 2019.

Sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee. His House website says he served as the committee's Vice-Chair before being named Chairman of its Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations; he is also a member of the Health and Environment subcommittees (Vice-Chairman of Environment) and served on the China Task Force in 2020.
Co-Chair of the House GOP Doctors' Caucus, the Children's Health Care Caucus and the Skin Cancer Caucus, and Vice-Chair of the Diabetes Caucus, according to his House website.

Has volunteered at the St. Vincent DePaul Soup Kitchen in Altoona and served on the advisory boards of Penn State Altoona, the American Cancer Society and the United Way, according to his House website.

priorities.text: Says he is 'working to defend our Constitutional rights, rebuild our economy, improve our health care system, strengthen our national security, stand up for our farmers and agriculture community... and create American jobs for American workers.'
On health care, says he is 'fighting every day to make our health care system work better for American patients,' citing his 'Homegrown Health Care Initiative' to expand the pipeline of doctors.
On energy, says he is 'working to rollback burdensome regulations, lower energy costs for American families, and create family-sustaining energy jobs' in the region.

positions.summary: Supports rolling back energy regulations to lower costs and grow Pennsylvania's energy industry rather than accelerating a transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: In Congress, Dr. Joyce is working to rollback burdensome regulations, lower energy costs for American families, and create family-sustaining energy jobs in our region.

positions.summary: Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2019, which would have required background checks on private firearm transfers.
Voted no on the Elijah E. Cummings Lower Drug Costs Now Act, which sought to have Medicare negotiate drug prices and expand Medicare coverage.
Voted no on the American Dream and Promise Act of 2019, which sought to protect certain immigrants from removal and provide a path to permanent residency.

record.text: Vice Chair of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce for the 2025–2026 term, also serving on its Communications and Technology and Health subcommittees.
Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2019 (H.R. 8), which passed the House 240–190.
Voted no on the Elijah E. Cummings Lower Drug Costs Now Act (H.R. 3), which passed the House 230–192.

candidates.name: Beth Farnham
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Beth Farnham is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 13th District. A former credit analyst, pharmacy technician and Conewago Valley school board member who describes herself as a stay-at-home parent, she also ran against John Joyce in 2024. Her campaign materials emphasize democracy, reproductive freedom, affordability, universal health care and gun safety.

background.text: Grew up in Maryland and graduated from Annapolis Senior High School. Her campaign website says she is the child of an HVAC technician and a nurse, spent most of her childhood in a row home in Baltimore and attended public schools.

Earned an associate degree from Anne Arundel Community College (1992) and a bachelor's degree from Towson University (1996). Her campaign website describes her degree as Biology, French and Secondary Education and says she put herself through college as the only member of her immediate family to graduate.

Worked her way through college as a pharmacy technician, including at a fertility pharmacy, and later as an administrative assistant for a lift-equipment company and as a credit analyst for Bank of America, according to a 2024 WPSU interview.

Describes herself as a stay-at-home parent (13 years as of her 2024 interview). She says she and her husband, Rob, were Republicans before moving toward the Democratic Party after 2016; she says she registered as a Democrat in 2019.
Served on the Conewago Valley School District board, representing Region 2, leaving office in 2023.
Won the 2024 Democratic primary (98.8%) and lost the general election to Joyce, 25.8% to 74.1%.

Was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary (32,428 votes) and is running a second time against Joyce; the Altoona Mirror reports her platform includes raising the federal minimum wage, a national health care plan and reproductive-freedom legislation.

According to her campaign website, she and her husband married at Gettysburg Presbyterian Church, settled in Adams County and are raising their children there; Ballotpedia lists her residence as Conewago Township.

priorities.text: Lists Democracy, Reproductive Freedom, Affordability, Gun Safety, Public Education, Universal Healthcare, Immigration Reform, and the Environment as core campaign issues.
priorities.quote: It means everything to me to be a voice in Congress for our precious Democracy, Reproductive Freedom, Affordability, Gun Safety, Public Education, Universal Healthcare, Immigration Reform, the Environment, and more.

priorities.text: Pledges to defend the U.S. Constitution, pass term limits for Supreme Court justices and age limits for members of Congress, and hold in-person town halls in the district.
On affordability, pledges to substantially increase the federal minimum wage, reduce tax cuts for the wealthy, and end Citizens United.

positions.summary: Pledges to enshrine reproductive freedom, including abortion access, into federal law.
positions.quote: Only when we have agency over our own bodies are we free to create the families we choose. With Reproductive Freedom, we, along with our trusted healthcare professionals, make personal and private medical decisions such as: abortion, birth control, disease prevention, nutrition, exercise, in vitro fertilization (IVF), and gender-affirming care.

positions.summary: Pledges to substantially increase the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: Substantially increase the federal minimum wage.

positions.summary: Pledges to sharply reduce tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy.
positions.quote: Sharply reduce tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy.

positions.summary: Lists universal health care as a core policy priority.
Lists gun safety among her core campaign issues.
